requirement: Build a Typer command that describes a service, validating the port range, a case-insensitive output format choice, and repeatable KEY=VALUE labels before any output is produced.
skeleton: A Format StrEnum, a validate_labels callback raising BadParameter, and a describe command with ranged port, enum format and repeatable label options producing JSON or tab-separated output.
caption: A single-command Typer app that validates its options declaratively before the command body runs. Format is a StrEnum of json and table. describe NAME takes --port limited to 1 through 65535 with min and max, --format chosen case-insensitively and defaulting to table, and a repeatable --label/-l whose callback validate_labels raises typer.BadParameter saying expected KEY=VALUE when an item has no equals sign or an empty key, so each violation exits with code 2. Labels split on the first equals sign so values may contain more. JSON output dumps name, port and labels with sorted keys; table output prints name, port and the labels sorted by key as k=v joined by commas, separated by tabs. The fixture asserts, with CliRunner, the default table output with sorted labels, case-insensitive JSON output keeping a value containing an equals sign, the port range edges, that labels missing the equals sign or key exit 2 with the message on stderr, and that an unknown format exits 2.

plan.intent: Validate CLI input before acting on it
constraints: Ports outside 1 through 65535 exit with code 2
The format choice is case-insensitive and defaults to table
Malformed labels raise typer.BadParameter so the command exits with code 2
Labels split on the first equals sign and print sorted by key

rationale.teaches: Push validation into Typer parameter declarations: min and max ranges, enum choices with case_sensitive=False, and a callback raising BadParameter.
rationale.why: Validating by hand inside the body produces tracebacks instead of usage errors, strict case matching rejects natural input, and naive splitting corrupts values containing separators.

ops.docstring: Validate Typer options with ranges, enum choices and a parameter callback.

candidates.why_wrong: Port 0 and 65536 are accepted instead of failing with a usage error.
An uppercase JSON format value is rejected as an invalid choice.
A label with an empty key such as =front passes validation.
Labels split on the last equals sign so url=a=b gets the wrong key.
Without --format the command prints JSON instead of the table layout.
